title: Fragmentation of Quantum Fluid in dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate
abstract: In this article, we study the dipolar Bosonic quantum fluid. The fluid experiences mean-field, beyond mean-field, and three body interactions. We investigate their competition with dipolar interaction and fragmentation as a result of this competition. We further investigate the elementary excitations and note two distinct dispersion regimes, namely roton-mode and modulational instability. We support our observation by calculating the superfluid fraction and the condensate fraction.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how competing interactions (mean-field, three-body, and dipolar) cause a quantum fluid in a dipolar BEC to fragment. The research predicts a roton instability, marking a transition into a super-solid phase, which is evidenced by measurable changes in the superfluid and condensate fractions.
main_problem: The study investigates the fragmentation of a quantum fluid within a dipolar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) due to the competition among various interaction types.
main_result: The system can undergo a roton instability, signaling a phase transition from a superfluid state to a super-solid or crystalline array, which is confirmed by changes in superfluid and condensate fractions.
method: The analysis employs theoretical modeling using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, analyzing the Bogoliubov spectrum to determine excitation modes and stability.
model_or_system: The physical system is a dipolar BEC, modeled in a quasi-one-dimensional geometry. The Hamiltonian incorporates mean-field, beyond mean-field, three-body, and non-local dipole-dipole interactions.
key_observables: Superfluid fraction ($f_s$), condensate fraction ($f_c$), excitation dispersion relation ($\Omega(k)$), and density modulation.
important_parameters: Dipolar interaction strength ($\epsilon_{dd}$ or $g_{dd}$), Mean-Field (MF) interaction strength, and particle number ($N_{at}$).
main_assumptions: The system is treated in a quasi-one-dimensional (Q1D) geometry, and the analysis relies on linear stability theory (Bogoliubov spectrum).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate density profiles showing fragmentation, dispersion relations highlighting roton minima and instability regions, and plots showing $f_s$ and $f_c$ changing as interaction strengths or particle numbers are varied.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the theoretical framework by incorporating multiple interaction terms into the governing equation, followed by detailed analysis of the excitation spectrum, superfluid/condensate fractions, and the resulting phase transitions (roton instability $ightarrow$ supersolid).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the complex many-body physics of dipolar quantum gases, linking interaction competition to exotic phases like supersolids and providing quantitative diagnostics ($f_s, f_c$) for these transitions.
